source: curated verified open-source repos that the live GitHub search can't reach from a locked-down sandbox. Each is a real, maintained project.

components.name: grbl
components.what: The classic G-code motion controller firmware for the ATmega328 (Arduino Uno). Runs a small CNC/plotter/laser from G-code.

components.name: FluidNC
components.what: Modern GRBL-style firmware for the ESP32 with Wi-Fi, a web UI, and config.yaml. Great if you want wireless control.

components.name: Marlin
components.what: The dominant 3D-printer/CNC firmware; also drives plotters and laser rigs. Heavier than GRBL but very capable.

components.name: Universal Gcode Sender (UGS)
components.what: Cross-platform Java host that streams G-code to GRBL/TinyG/FluidNC over USB, with jogging, visualizer, and macros.

components.name: CNCjs
components.what: A web-based G-code sender/controller (Node.js) for GRBL/Smoothie/TinyG; runs in the browser, great on a Raspberry Pi.

components.name: bCNC
components.what: Python/Tk GRBL sender with a strong toolpath editor, autoleveling, and G-code utilities.

components.name: vpype
components.what: The Swiss-army knife for pen-plotter vector art: load/optimize/transform SVG, then export. Pairs with vpype-gcode.

components.name: vpype-gcode
components.what: vpype plugin that writes G-code from optimized vector paths, with configurable pen-up/pen-down commands.

components.name: juicy-gcode
components.what: Command-line SVG-to-G-code converter with good Bezier handling and a configurable flavor for pen plotters.
